issues.body:
Parent roadmap: #46. Phase: implementation, before owner Deck tests.

## Outcome

Make a normal Decky ZIP the primary install/update unit while retaining the working Go core and current OBSGod compatibility identity. The SDK, Python backend, bundled Go helper and native capture payload already exist; align packaging and remove mandatory dependence on the separately installed Desktop application.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document and implement the supported source/build entry point using the current official Decky template/CLI conventions, with pinned reproducible tooling; retain justified license boundaries rather than blindly replacing Rollup.
- [ ] A clean build produces a directly installable ZIP with correct top-level folder, manifests, dist/index.js, Python backend, bundled Go helper, native capture library, assets and required notices/preferred source.
- [ ] The normal Decky ZIP alone contains everything our plugin needs for its own setup UI; OBS/GStreamer remain external Flatpak dependencies.
- [ ] Use ordinary player privileges, supplied Decky context, and no root/debug flags or SteamOS read-only unlock.
- [ ] Preserve obsgod/OBSGod plugin/command/update compatibility while building and testing under szmyty/obsgod; the future repository is deckystream, with owner still unresolved.
- [ ] Check source/native ABI consumers separately and verify the official build/output path plus ZIP contents; archive checks do not establish actual Deck installation.
- [ ] Inspect workflow side effects and prepare version metadata without triggering a product release, deployment or Store submission.

## Verification

Clean build, package schema/path/payload/license checks, deterministic repeated output where promised, and an unpacked backend smoke. Actual normal-UI install is covered by the owner test gate.

## Dependencies and original scope

Can start independently after reconciling the existing draft stack #73 → #74 → #75. Original related ledgers: #19, #20, #22, #44, #45. Their complete criteria/dependencies remain under #46; this bounded issue does not replace or pass them.

Existing source, including shared legacy/API and Linux package work in #75, must be reused. Old receipts qualify only their recorded revisions. This issue starts as planned work, not an implementation or acceptance claim.

issues.title: Add consented OBS/GStreamer setup with progress, cancel and retry
issues.summary: After Decky installs the plugin, offer recoverable dependency setup in the plugin itself. Current dependency installation exists only in the Desktop installer; the plugin's _main currently initializes permissions and the runtime only checks dependencies.
criteria: Opening the plugin observes dependency readiness and offers an Install/Later consent UI listing OBS, its compatible GStreamer extension and any required Flathub setup. _main/_migration never start dependency downloads.
Declining leaves the plugin installed with a clear Setup required screen, help and explicit retry; streaming stays unavailable with the actual missing-dependency reason.

Run a backend-owned asynchronous setup job with operation identity, bounded diagnostics/progress and a multi-minute budget separate from stream-operation timeouts. Closing/reopening the panel recovers status without duplicate work.
Cancellation, interruption, reload and failures re-observe installed refs; retry only missing work. Do not assume an interrupted Flatpak transaction installed nothing or delete its cache/shared apps.

Verify actual player UID/home/session bus, user versus system scope, compatible active OBS/add-on branches, OBS 28+ bundled WebSocket capability, and the identity of an existing flathub remote. Never overwrite an unrelated remote, silently create a duplicate installation, install a second WebSocket plugin or unlock SteamOS.
Handle offline network, disk exhaustion, missing Flatpak, permissions and incompatible versions with actionable recovery; keep ordinary OBS and shared dependencies intact.
Dependency installed, managed OBS launched, authenticated listener ready and stream active are separate observed states. Setup cannot broadcast.
issues.validation: Job/lifecycle/consent/cancel/retry and partial-ref fixtures, failure redaction and duplicate prevention. Mark Gaming Mode Flatpak installation unrun until exercised on the actual Deck.

issues.title: Complete private first-run configuration inside the Decky panel
issues.summary: Let the normal plugin configure its existing provider/RTMP presets and managed OBS connection without requiring the paired Desktop application. Reuse the existing robust Go Configure path; OAuth/QR account login is a separate research track.
criteria: Provide controller-usable setup/settings for Kick, Twitch and existing supported RTMP(S) destinations, with sensible defaults and validation. Manual stream-key input remains fully supported offline after configuration.

Mask keys by default; integrate normal keyboard/paste behavior and an optional documented Desktop entry path for easier typing, without requiring a separately installed app or exposing an unauthenticated LAN service.
Reuse current binding semantics: blank means keep a stored key only for the same destination; changing the server/account destination cannot silently reuse another key.
Keep destination stream key, local setup authorization and managed OBS WebSocket password distinct. Generate/store the managed password privately; support the existing safe recovery/change behavior.
Saving, testing readiness or recording a local test never starts broadcasting. Unsafe active/unknown output changes retain existing stop/confirmation behavior.
Preserve current CLI/file/environment precedence and existing profiles without using an environment variable to change branding, update trust or compatibility IDs.
Diagnostics, receipts, support export, frontend readback and clipboard-copy logs never reveal stream keys, OBS passwords or private setup tokens.
issues.validation: Synthetic key sentinel/binding/recovery tests, setup UI keyboard/focus checks, save/readback redaction and offline repeat setup. Real Kick viewer proof remains in the owner test gate.

issues.summary: Let Decky own ordinary plugin replacement/removal and retire the mandatory paired installer/updater path safely. Existing Desktop helpers may remain bounded recovery tools; do not replace the normal Decky channel with internal backend automation.

Provide inventory/preview-driven removal of obsolete OBSGod-owned launchers/app/helper data after successful transition, with rollback/export before any explicit wipe.
Normal removal preserves settings, recordings/history, ordinary OBS, other plugins and shared OBS/GStreamer dependencies. Reset and complete owned-data wipe require their separate explicit scope.
Unknown/active outputs cannot be treated as safe idle by our cleanup tools; preserve existing stop/confirmation and safe-path identity checks.
Qualify new lifecycle code against current szmyty/obsgod artifacts; actual new publisher transition is a later exact-destination task.
issues.validation: Normal loader lifecycle fixtures or free supported local execution, old/current repair/rollback/uninstall fixtures, abrupt interruption and unrelated-data sentinels. Record actual loader/Deck checks unrun until owner testing.

issues.title: Research Twitch/Kick OAuth and phone QR login as a separate mini-roadmap
issues.summary: Separate optional account-login research from the current implementation. Reuse the auth intent preserved from consolidated #14/#40 under #46, without reopening their broader companion/ecosystem scope or blocking manual-key streaming.
criteria: Record official provider support, endpoints/scopes, client type/registration ownership and prerequisites. Start from docs/authentication-options.md and recheck sources before a design decision.

Twitch journey: assess public-client Device Code Grant, a QR of Twitch's verification URI, user code, polling/expiry/denial/cancel, channel:read:stream_key and authorized broadcaster key retrieval. Document that OBS still uses ingest URL/key internally.

Kick journey: resolve documented authorization-code + PKCE client-secret requirements, actual streamkey:read/channel scope/key visibility and whether a provider-supported public/native/device option exists. Do not embed a shared confidential secret or invent a secretless/device flow.
Distinguish provider device QR, a local setup-page QR and authorization-code callback/pairing. Phone localhost is the phone; do not expose an unauthenticated local configuration server.
Compare private token/key storage, validation/serialized refresh/revocation, account switching, offline/manual fallback and any proposed broker's ownership/privacy/cost before choosing a design.
Prepare the real Deck+phone/account evidence plan and precise owner actions, then discuss/select the design with the owner before creating authentication implementation work.

Keep account registration, production credentials, auth coding, live streams, hosting/deployment, payments and Store contact outside this research issue. No successful account/device/ingest test is claimed by documentation research.
issues.validation: Source-backed feasibility/decision packet and future test checklist. Current Twitch/Kick registration, OAuth, key retrieval, phone/Deck and live-ingest flows remain unrun.
